history.dynasty: Kalchuri, 11th century — single uncorroborated claim (see summary)
history.period: Ancient temple near the dam; the dam itself is modern (see summary)
history.summary: A Lord Shiva shrine stands by the Khutaghat Dam (Sanjay Gandhi Reservoir) on the Kharang river, about 6-7 km from Ratanpur in Bilaspur district (chhattisgarhpedia). Its signature feature: the temple is submerged under the reservoir and can only be reached in summer when water levels recede. CONFLICTS: antiquity — one now-offline temple site claimed an 11th-century Kalchuri origin, but no other source corroborates this, so treat it as unverified; the dam's construction date is given as 1930 by chhattisgarhpedia but 1973-1984 by another source (koreatripguide, which carries other inconsistencies such as a 1984 inauguration by a President who left office in 1982); the distance from Bilaspur is reported as 32 km (chhattisgarhpedia) versus 15-16 km (a travel blogger); the river is named Kharang, Kharoon or Khudi in different sources. CSV CORRECTION: town 'Bilaspur' is approximate — the dam is near Ratanpur, Bilaspur district; corrected to Ratanpur. Coordinates are a Ratanpur landmark approximation (no POI-level geocode match for the temple). No festival is documented for this shrine; Mahashivratri observance is likely but unconfirmed.

name: Khutaghat Dam Temple
town_description: Ratanpur, about 25 km from Bilaspur, was the capital of the Kalachuri kings of Ratnapura and is known as the city of temples and ponds. Its Mahamaya temple is one of the 52 Shakti Peethas, and Khutaghat Dam is its nearby picnic and pilgrimage spot.

travel.airport: Bilaspur airport is the nearest (per chhattisgarhpedia).
travel.railway: Bilaspur railway station is the nearest (per chhattisgarhpedia).
travel.road: On the Bilaspur-Ambikapur highway; reachable by bike or taxi from Bilaspur. A Tourist Rest House built by the Chhattisgarh government is near the dam.

visitor_information.best_time: Summer (low-water months) for the temple, which is accessible only when water levels recede; monsoon for the dam's scenery.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Temple access depends on reservoir levels (summer only, per chhattisgarhpedia); boating 9 AM-4 PM; dam area open sunrise to sunset.
